extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (practitioners advising on priority/benefit claims)
extracted.subtask_short: claiming benefit of earlier filing date
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for when a later-filed U.S. (or national-stage) application may be entitled to the filing date of an earlier application (provisional, nonprovisional, or international). Covers statutory requirements, timing, required references, disclosures, petition procedures for delayed claims, and examiner form-paragraph usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reference requirement to earlier-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: No application shall be entitled to the benefit of an earlier filed application under this section unless an amendment containing the specific reference to the earlier filed application is submitted at such time during the pendency of the application as required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference must identify the prior application by application number (series code + serial number) or international application number and international filing date and indicate the relationship of the applications. The Director may consider failure to submit such an amendment within the required time period as a waiver of any benefit; the Director may establish procedures, including payment of a surcharge, to accept an unintentionally delayed submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional-to-nonprovisional 12‑month filing rule (35 U.S.C. 119(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (or 363) that relies on a provisional application must be filed not later than 12 months after the provisional application was filed and must contain or be amended to contain a specific reference to the provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 12‑month anniversary falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the period is extended to the next succeeding business day. The nonprovisional must contain the reference during pendency as required by the Director; failure to timely submit the reference is considered a waiver (unless petitioned as unintentionally delayed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application reliance requires payment of specified fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) may not be relied upon in any proceeding in the Patent and Trademark Office unless the fee set forth in subparagraph (A) or (C) of section 41(a)(1) has been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the basic filing fee (per applicable rule) was not paid as required, reliance on the provisional is precluded; abandonment of the provisional for failure to pay the basic filing fee would indicate the nonprovisional cannot claim the benefit of the provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph) for benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application must disclose the claimed invention of the later-filed application in the manner provided by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description and enablement) for a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure must provide adequate support and enablement to permit one of ordinary skill in the art to make and use the claimed invention without undue experimentation. Example: New Railhead — where a provisional lacked explicit support for an 'angled' limitation, the later patent was not entitled to the provisional date. If the prior disclosure is insufficient, the later-filed claim is not entitled to the earlier filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship requirement for benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Each prior-filed application relied upon must name as an inventor at least one inventor named in the later-filed application and disclose the named inventor’s invention claimed in at least one claim of the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is explicit in 37 CFR 1.78(a)(1) and is necessary for benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) and also for 119(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior application filing‑date entitlement and fee condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior-filed application relied upon must be: (i) an international application entitled to a filing date in accordance with PCT Article 11 and designating the U.S., or (ii) entitled to a filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 1.53(d) and have paid the basic filing fee set forth in §1.16 within the pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these conditions are not met, the earlier application cannot provide the filing date benefit. See also provisions regarding payment of basic filing fee for provisional applications (§1.16(d) / §1.53(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and nonextendable deadlines for submitting reference to prior application (37 CFR 1.78(a)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for a continued prosecution application filed under §1.53(d), a later-filed application claiming benefit must contain or be amended to contain a reference to each prior application and this reference must be submitted during the pendency of the later-filed application and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the later-filed application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national-stage applications entering from an international application, analogous later-of-four-months-or-sixteen-months periods apply measured from the national stage commencement date or the prior filing date. These time periods are not extendable. Exceptions apply for design applications, applications filed before November 29, 2000, and certain national-stage timing circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format/placement of reference in nonprovisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the later-filed application is a nonprovisional application, the reference required must be included in an application data sheet (§1.76), or the specification must contain or be amended to contain such reference in the first sentence(s) following the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisionals, failure to include the reference in the ADS or immediately after the title may cause a waiver if not timely corrected. Use ADS (§1.76) to list related applications where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements for unintentionally delayed benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is presented after the required time period, a claim for the benefit of the earlier filing date may be accepted if the delay was unintentional and a petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be accompanied by: (i) the required reference (unless previously submitted), (ii) the surcharge set forth in §1.17(t), and (iii) a statement that the entire delay between the date the claim was due and the date the claim was filed was unintentional. The Director may require additional information where there is a question as to unintentionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and accuracy statement requirement for non‑English provisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior-filed provisional application was filed in a language other than English and both an English-language translation and a statement that the translation is accurate were not previously filed in the provisional, applicant will be notified and given a period to file them in the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notice is mailed in a pending nonprovisional application, a timely reply must include either confirmation that the translation and statement were filed in the provisional, or an amendment or Supplemental ADS withdrawing the benefit claim, or the nonprovisional application will be abandoned. The translation and statement may be filed in the provisional even if it has become abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copendency requirement for nonprovisional benefit claims (35 U.S.C.120/121/365(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming the benefit of a prior nonprovisional under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c), the later-filed application must be copending with the prior application (filed before patenting, abandonment, or termination of proceedings in the prior application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copendency is satisfied if the later-filed application is filed on the same date the prior issues or before the patent issues. If proceedings in the prior application are terminated (e.g., mandate issued after affirmance), the later application must have been filed before that termination to be copending. If not copending, the later-filed application is not entitled to the benefit and prior art is judged from its actual filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/divisional disclosure sameness and new matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure of a continuation application must be the same as the disclosure of the prior-filed application. The disclosure of a divisional application must be the same as, or include that portion of the disclosure of the prior-filed application that is germane to the invention claimed in the divisional. A continuation or divisional cannot include anything which would constitute new matter if inserted in the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application purports to be a continuation or divisional but contains matter not in the prior application, the relationship must be changed to continuation-in-part; see use of form paragraph 2.10.01 to require change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-part (CIP) partial benefit rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation-in-part application may include matter not disclosed in the prior application. Only claims in the CIP that are disclosed in the manner provided by 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, in the prior-filed application are entitled to the benefit of the filing date of the prior-filed application; other claims are entitled only to the CIP filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CIP claims that are only entitled to the CIP filing date read on published or publicly used subject matter, a 35 U.S.C. 102 rejection would be proper. Cases cited include In re Chu, Transco Products, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when claims are not entitled to earlier filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims in the later-filed application are not entitled to the benefit of an earlier filing date, the examiner should notify applicant that one or more conditions have not been satisfied and conduct a prior art search based on the actual filing date of the application instead of the earlier filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may use an intervening reference in a rejection until applicant corrects the benefit claim or shows that the conditions have been met. The effective filing date for prior-art purposes is the actual filing date of the later-filed application. Use form paragraph 2.09 and related paragraphs to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and examiner procedural guidance for benefit-claim defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraphs (e.g., 2.09, 2.10, 2.10.01, 2.38–2.40) to notify applicant when claims are not entitled to an earlier filing date due to lack of support/enablement or presence of new matter, and to instruct on required corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶2.10: Disclosure of prior-filed application does not provide support for claimed subject matter; ¶2.10.01: continuation/divisional contains new matter and must be changed to CIP. Follow examiner notes in each form paragraph (insert prior application number, explain lack of support, list claims not entitled to benefit, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of application by application number includes all applications assigned that number
rubrics_metrics.description: The identification of an application by application number under this section is the identification of every application assigned that application number necessary for a specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 to every such application assigned that application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referencing by application number, be aware that the number may be assigned to multiple related applications and the reference should be understood as identifying each such application as appropriate for the specific reference requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and historical rule changes affecting benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain exceptions apply to the timing and copendency rules (e.g., applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before November 29, 2000; nonprovisionals entering national stage from internationals filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before November 29, 2000). Public Law 106-113 amended 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) to eliminate the copendency requirement for nonprovisionals claiming the benefit of provisionals (effective Nov. 29, 1999 for provisionals filed on or after June 8, 1995).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply historical-effective-date rules carefully: some older applications enjoy different timing/copendency treatment. Also note that while copendency was eliminated for certain provisional‑benefit claims, abandonment of the provisional for failure to pay the basic filing fee may nonetheless bar benefit claims.
